title: Forge 10: RNN with backprop through time, and a GRU cell

wrong.no_recurrent_gradient.py: BPTT stops after one step: dh never flows to the previous hidden state, so early inputs get no gradient
wrong.tanh_derivative_slip.py: the tanh derivative is taken as 1 - h instead of 1 - h^2
wrong.overwrite_over_time.py: dWxh is assigned at every step, so only the earliest time step survives instead of the sum over time
wrong.whh_grad_uses_new_state.py: dWhh pairs the gradient with h_t instead of h_{t-1}
wrong.state_carried_over.py: the hidden state is not reset: the previous call's last state leaks into the next sequence
wrong.mean_over_batch.py: dWhy is averaged over the batch; that scaling belongs to the loss
wrong.gru_swapped_gate.py: h' = z*n + (1-z)*h (the gate convention flipped): forward and backward agree with each other but not with the spec
wrong.gru_missing_reset_gradient.py: the reset gate gets no gradient, so Wx_r, Wh_r and b_r are never trained
wrong.gru_sigmoid_derivative.py: the update gate's sigmoid derivative drops the (1 - z) factor
wrong.gru_forgets_direct_path.py: dh omits the direct z * dh_new path, so the gradient cannot skip through an open update gate
wrong.gru_grads_accumulate.py: dWx accumulates across backward calls instead of being set

hints: Forward: keep the list of hidden states h_0..h_T (h_0 = zeros). You need h_{t-1} and h_t at every step during backward, so cache all of them, not just the last.

Backward starts at the end: dh = dlogits @ Why.T, dWhy = h_T.T @ dlogits, dby = sum over the batch. Then walk t = T-1 down to 0: da = dh * (1 - h_{t+1}**2) is the gradient at the pre-activation, because d tanh(a)/da = 1 - tanh(a)**2.

The weights are shared across time, so each step ADDS to dWxh (x_t.T @ da), dWhh (h_{t-1}.T @ da) and dbh (sum of da). The gradient handed to the previous step is dh = da @ Whh.T, and dx_t = da @ Wxh.T. Start the three accumulators at zero inside backward so repeated calls do not pile up.

GRU backward, working back from h' = (1 - z)*n + z*h: dn = dh'*(1-z), dz = dh'*(h-n), and h also receives dh'*z directly. Then through the activations: da_n = dn*(1-n**2); da_z = dz*z*(1-z); the reset gate only touches the candidate through r * (h Wh_n), so dr = da_n * (h Wh_n) and da_r = dr*r*(1-r).

Pack the gate gradients like the weights: da = [da_z | da_r | da_n] for x, but for h the third block is da_n * r because the candidate sees r * (h Wh_n). Then dWx = x.T @ da, dWh = h.T @ dah, db = da.sum(0), dx = da @ Wx.T and dh = dh'*z + dah @ Wh.T. A finite-difference check on dh and on the reset gate's weights finds most slips.
